_comment: Hydrology seed entries (same shape as seed_catalog.json). USGS NWIS (the main US source behind CUAHSI HIS) and PO.DAAC Hydrocron endpoints, Giovanni IDs (tests/fixtures/recorded/giovanni_configured_variables.json), CMR concept IDs, DOIs and UMM-Var units were checked live on 2026-11-14. Definitions are editorial plain-language text for students.

variables.name: River streamflow at a USGS stream gauge (US)
variables.short_definition: How much water flows past a river gauge every second, measured by the U.S. Geological Survey.
variables.definition: Streamflow (discharge) is the volume of water passing a point of a river each second. USGS gauges measure the water level many times a day and turn it into flow with a rating curve checked by field measurements. We use the daily means and average them to months; a month counts only if at least 70% of its days have values. Days that USGS marks as ice-affected, equipment failure, discontinued or missing are left out, never filled in. For a point we use the nearest gauge (within about 25-50 km); for a box, the gauge with the largest drainage area (the most downstream one). United States only. This is the same USGS data that CUAHSI HIS serves.
variables.verified_note: NWIS dv, NWIS site service and the OGC API daily collection checked live on 2026-11-14 (site 01646500, Potomac River).

dataset.variable: 00060 Discharge, cubic feet per second (daily mean)

variables.coverage_note: Depends on the gauge; many US gauges start before 1950.

variables.name: River water level (gage height) at a USGS gauge (US)
variables.short_definition: How high the water stands in a river at a gauge, above the gauge's own zero mark.
variables.definition: Gage height (stage) is the height of the water surface above a fixed reference point at the gauge, called the gauge datum. It is not height above sea level. USGS sometimes moves a gauge or resets its datum; that shows up as a sudden step in the record, so a step should be read as a possible instrument effect, not a change in the river. Daily means are averaged to months (a month needs 70% of its days). Values flagged as ice-affected, equipment failure or missing are left out. United States only.
variables.verified_note: Same USGS services as usgs_streamflow, checked live on 2026-11-14; parameter 00065 is the standard NWIS gage height code.

variables.name: Lake or reservoir water level at a USGS gauge (US)
variables.short_definition: How high the water surface of a lake or reservoir stands, measured by the U.S. Geological Survey.
variables.definition: The elevation of a lake or reservoir surface above a vertical reference (NGVD 1929, NAVD 1988 or a local datum). Reservoir levels go up and down with rainfall, snowmelt, water use and dam operations, so a trend can reflect management as well as climate. We use the first available of USGS parameters 62614 (above NGVD 1929), 62615 (above NAVD 1988) and 00062 (reservoir elevation), and never mix two datums in one series; the one used is listed in the provenance. Daily values are averaged to months (a month needs 70% of its days). United States only.
variables.verified_note: Parameters 62614 and 62615 checked live on 2026-11-14 (e.g. 08104650 Lake Georgetown, TX). No site with 00062 daily values was found in the tested box, so that code is unverified.

dataset.variable: 62614 / 62615 / 00062 Lake or reservoir water surface elevation, feet

variables.name: River streamflow, modelled (NLDAS, US only)
variables.short_definition: Monthly river flow estimated by a land-surface computer model on a grid over the United States.
variables.definition: NLDAS-2 runs the Noah land-surface model with observed rain, sun and temperature to estimate where water goes. Streamflow here is model output for one 1/8-degree grid cell, not a measurement, so compare it with a USGS gauge when you can. Pick a point on a large river: the flow of a grid cell depends on which rivers pass through it, so this variable is not averaged over boxes. Continental United States only, monthly from 1979.
variables.verified_note: Giovanni ID in the recorded /configured-variables listing (2026-11-14); CMR concept C1887990023-GES_DISC, DOI and UMM-Var (Streamflow, m^3 sec-1, fill -9999) checked live; CMR granules list Cloud OPeNDAP URLs. Harmony area averaging not needed (point only); the OPeNDAP DMR itself was not opened (needs an Earthdata token).

variables.name: Baseflow from groundwater (GLDAS model)
variables.short_definition: Water that seeps out of the ground into streams, keeping rivers flowing between rains.
variables.definition: Baseflow (subsurface runoff) is the slow part of river flow that comes from soil and groundwater rather than from rain running over the surface. It is model output from GLDAS Noah, in kg m-2 (1 kg m-2 equals 1 mm of water). Falling baseflow can point to drier soils or less groundwater recharge. Land only.
variables.verified_note: Both Giovanni IDs in the recorded /configured-variables listing (2026-11-14); concept IDs, DOI (3H) and UMM-Var units (Qsb_acc, kg m-2) checked in CMR. Monthly DOI is 10.5067/SXAVCZFAQLNO.

variables.name: River water surface height from the SWOT satellite
variables.short_definition: The height of a river's water surface above sea level, measured from space by the SWOT satellite.
variables.definition: SWOT (Surface Water and Ocean Topography, launched December 2022) measures water heights with a radar that looks at a wide swath. It sees each river reach (a stretch of about 10 km) only a few times every 21 days, from July 2023 on. Monthly values are the average of the passes in that month. The record is only a few years long, which is too short to test for a long-term trend yet: use it to see seasons and floods, and to compare with river gauges. Needs a SWORD reach id (options.feature_id).
variables.verified_note: Hydrocron /timeseries checked live on 2026-11-14 (reach 78340600051, collection_name pinned); CMR concept and DOI checked.

variables.name: Lake water surface height from the SWOT satellite
variables.short_definition: The height of a lake's water surface above sea level, measured from space by the SWOT satellite.
variables.definition: SWOT measures the water height of lakes and reservoirs from space, a few times every 21 days since July 2023. Monthly values are the average of the passes in that month. The record is only a few years long, which is too short to test for a long-term trend yet: use it to see seasonal filling and emptying, and to compare with USGS reservoir gauges. Needs a Prior Lake Database (PLD) lake id (options.feature_id).
variables.verified_note: Hydrocron /timeseries checked live on 2026-11-14 (lake 6350036102, collection_name pinned); CMR concept and DOI checked.
